images.filename: F-4C Phantoms with AIM-7 missiles at Cam Ranh 1967.jpg
images.caption: U.S. Air Force ground personnel prepare AIM-7E Sparrow missiles for loading on McDonnell F-4C Phantom II aircraft (s/n 63-7473, 64-0830) at an air base in South Vietnam, in 1967. 63-7473 is armed with a 20 mm gun pod and napalm canisters. Note that 64-0830 is not equipped with the IR-sensor. It served with the 559th Tactical Fighter Squadron, 12th Tactical Fighter Wing at Cam Ranh Air Base. It crashed in Laos on 22 March 1968 following a bomb malfunction over Khe Sanh. One crew member was captured, the other is missing.
images.alt: U.S. Air Force ground personnel prepare AIM-7E Sparrow missiles for loading on McDonnell F-4C Phantom II aircraft (s/n 63-7473, 64-0830) at an air base in South Vietnam, in 1967. 63-7473 is armed with a 20 mm gun pod and napalm canisters. Note that 64-0830 is not equipped with the IR-sensor. It served with the 559th Tactical Fighter Squadron, 12th Tactical Fighter Wing at Cam Ranh Air Base. It crashed in Laos on 22 March 1968 following a bomb malfunction over Khe Sanh. One crew member was captured, the other is missing.

images.filename: Two former U.S. Navy type T2 tankers used at power stations at Cam Ranh Bay, 3 September 1966 (RN 735-17c).jpg
images.caption: Two former U.S. Navy type T2 tankers at Cam Ranh Bay, 3 September 1966. Two of the vessels shown in the foreground of this at Cam Ranh Bay supplied power for the Cam Ranh Bay complex, the third one (left) delivered fuel oil. The primary distribution lines from the tankers to the depot in the distant background had been completed. This represened 5% of the land distribution system that was installed at Cam Ranh Bay. The third T-2 tanker was scheduled to arrive at Cam Ranh Bay before 15 October 1966 and the entire land distribution system was scheduled to be finished in January 1967.
images.alt: Two former U.S. Navy type T2 tankers at Cam Ranh Bay, 3 September 1966. Two of the vessels shown in the foreground of this at Cam Ranh Bay supplied power for the Cam Ranh Bay complex, the third one (left) delivered fuel oil. The primary distribution lines from the tankers to the depot in the distant background had been completed. This represened 5% of the land distribution system that was installed at Cam Ranh Bay.
